title: Induction by enlarging a fixed quasi-compact open of an algebraic space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: every open cover has a finite subcover and the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Let $W_0\subset X$ be a quasi-compact open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace], and let $\mathcal P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of quasi-compact open subspaces of $X$. An elementary distinguished square $(W_1\subset W_2,f:V\to W_2)$ means an open immersion $W_1\to W_2$, a representable etale map $f$, and an isomorphism $V\times_{W_2}Z\to Z$, where $Z$ is the reduced closed subspace with underlying set $|W_2|\setminus|W_1|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]; underlying point sets carry the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume (i) $\mathcal P(W_0)$; and (ii) for every such square with $W_1,W_2$ quasi-compact open in $X$, $W_0\subset W_1$, and $V$ an affine scheme, $\mathcal P(W_1)$ implies $\mathcal P(W_2)$. Then $\mathcal P(X)$ holds. In every square quantified over in (ii), $H=W_1\times_{W_2}V$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of $V$.

source.place: Tag 09IT, lemma-induction-principle-enlarge; its distinguished-square setting and the quasi-compact overlap observation in the proof of lemma-induction-principle.

proof.text: First verify the additional overlap assertion. For any square in (ii), the inclusion $W_1\to X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence], since $W_1$ is quasi-compact and $X$ is quasi-separated. Its pullback along the affine scheme $V\to W_2\to X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. This pullback equals $H=W_1\times_{W_2}V$, because $W_2\to X$ is a monomorphism. By [def-a1-space-open-subspace] it is represented by an open subscheme of $V$. The scheme-test clause of the quasi-compactness lemma therefore makes this open subscheme quasi-compact. This proves the overlap assertion for all the quantified squares, independently of $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 08GP (lemma-induction-principle), quasi-compact overlap observation; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 073B, 03HF, 03HD

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and then [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-splitting-filtration] to $j_!X$. This use is legitimate for arbitrary $S$: the former node identifies scheme atlases and their fibre products, and its equivalence identifies subspaces and their scheme tests. Hence open subspaces and their point topology, reduced closed subspaces, representable etale maps and quasi-compactness are unchanged. The absolute diagonal is the diagonal of this same space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, so it too is unchanged. Transporting the filtration back gives quasi-compact opens $\emptyset=U_{n+1}\subset U_n\subset\cdots\subset U_1=X$ and surjective representable etale maps $f_p:V_p\to U_p$, with $V_p$ quasi-compact separated schemes, isomorphic over the reduced complements $Z_p=U_p\setminus U_{p+1}$. Every transported chart has its map to $S$ by composition through $X$.

source.place: Tag 09IT (lemma-induction-principle-enlarge), first proof paragraph; decent-spaces.tex Tag 07ST; spaces.tex Tags 03I4, 04SG

proof.text: Set $A_p=W_0\cup U_p$. Finite unions of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact: restrict any open cover to each member, take finite subcovers there, and unite them. Thus $A_p$ lies in the domain of $\mathcal P$. We prove $\mathcal P(A_p)$ by descending induction on $p$. The initial value is $A_{n+1}=W_0$, covered by (i). Fix $p\le n$ and assume $\mathcal P(A_{p+1})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover], choose a finite affine open cover $V_p=\bigcup_{i=1}^{m}V_{p,i}$. Define $B_0=A_{p+1}$ and $B_i=A_{p+1}\cup\bigcup_{j\le i}f_p(V_{p,j})$. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] each image is a quasi-compact open subspace. Each $B_i$ is consequently a quasi-compact open containing $W_0$, and surjectivity of $f_p$ gives $B_m=A_p$.

source.place: Tag 09IT (lemma-induction-principle-enlarge), induction and finite affine-cover construction

proof.text: For $1\le i\le m$, the composite $V_{p,i}\to U_p\to X$ is representable etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Its image lies in $B_i$, so [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] factors it through $B_i$; the factor is also etale, being its base change along the open $B_i\to X$. Let $C_i$ be the reduced closed complement of $B_{i-1}$ in $B_i$, supplied by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Its support lies in $U_p\setminus U_{p+1}$: points outside $U_p$ or in $U_{p+1}$ already lie in $B_0$. Thus $C_i\to X$ factors through the open $U_p$. Moreover it factors through $Z_p$. Indeed, on etale affine charts the ideal of $Z_p$ is the radical ideal of that closed subset, as specified in the filtration node; its image in the reduced chart of $C_i$ vanishes in every residue field, hence belongs to every prime and is zero. These local factorizations are unique through the closed immersion, hence agree on overlaps. This is the explicit reduced-source factorization needed here.

source.place: Tag 09IT, enlarged and affine-refined squares; Tag 08GN (lemma-make-more-elementary-distinguished-squares), reduced-complement restriction argument

proof.text: The isomorphism $V_p\times_{U_p}Z_p\simeq Z_p$ of step 2, pulled back along $C_i\to Z_p$, identifies $V_p\times_{U_p}C_i$ with $C_i$. Every point of $C_i$ belongs to $f_p(V_{p,i})$: a point of $B_i$ outside $B_{i-1}$ can only have been added by this $i$th image. Under the preceding isomorphism, the open subspace $V_{p,i}\times_{U_p}C_i$ therefore has full point image in $C_i$, using the fibre-product image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The full-image open clause of that node makes it the whole of $C_i$. Since $C_i\to B_i\to X$ already factors through $U_p$, the fibre product just obtained also equals $V_{p,i}\times_{B_i}C_i$. Consequently $(B_{i-1}\subset B_i,V_{p,i}\to B_i)$ is an elementary distinguished square. This proves the square condition directly, rather than citing the omitted proof of Tag 08GN.

source.place: Tag 09IT, assertion that the affine-refined pairs are elementary distinguished squares; Tag 08GN (1), argument filled in

proof.text: Starting with $\mathcal P(B_0)=\mathcal P(A_{p+1})$, apply (ii) to the squares of steps 4--5 in increasing order of $i$. Their lower opens are quasi-compact, contain $W_0$, and their other charts $V_{p,i}$ are affine, so every hypothesis of (ii) holds. This finite induction gives $\mathcal P(B_m)=\mathcal P(A_p)$ and completes the descending induction. If the chosen affine cover is empty, $V_p$ is empty and its surjectivity implies $U_p=\emptyset$; then $A_p=A_{p+1}=W_0$ and no application of (ii) is needed. Finally $A_1=W_0\cup X=X$, hence $\mathcal P(X)$ holds. Together with step 1 this proves all clauses, including when $X$ is empty or $W_0=X$.

The statement matches 09IT hypothesis by hypothesis and is unchanged. Representable étale agrees with étale because V is an affine scheme. The overlap clause is the observation in the 08GP proof. Step 1: qcqs-permanence plus affine-tests plus the monomorphism W_2→X give H qc open. Step 2: the transport through j_! is justified by clauses (1)-(3) of the change-of-base node; qs is absolute by definition. Step 3: the induction claim is P(W_0∪U_p) with base W_0, and the report correctly names the source typo (∩ should be ∪); B_m = A_p is checked. Step 4: |C_i| ⊂ U_p\U_{p+1}; C_i factors through Z_p by reducedness and the radical-ideal charts, which is an elementary argument. Step 5: pulling back the filtration isomorphism and the full-image clause of point-open-calculus prove 08GN(1) for this case. Step 6: every hypothesis of (ii) is checked, including empty covers. Edge cases tested: X=∅, W_0=X, V_p=∅. Not a duplicate of the 08GP node lem-sfb-space-qcqs-distinguished-square-induction. proof_deps equals the union of uses, there is no cycle and no SGA citation.
